newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares stalled amid Christmas lull.
newsitem.headline: German shares stalled amid Christmas lull.

text.p: The fast-approaching Christmas holiday put a brake on German stock market activity on Monday, leaving blue chip shares to trade on very thin volumes and in tight ranges.
The 30-share DAX index limped its way to a lower close in the floor session, dropping 8.88 points to end at 2,845.57, after hovering in a range of just seven points.
All-day electronic dealings ended with the IBIS DAX index at 2,844.09, 8.55 points above the late close on Friday.
Dealers said volumes were markedly weak and that no clear trend emerged. Many market participants were already off, with German financial markets to close Tuesday through Thursday.
"At least we've got Solitaire here," said a trader on the Frankfurt bourse. "There is absolutely nothing else to do."
"We should have given ourselves today off as a Christmas present," said a Duesseldorf dealer.
Deutsche Bank slipped in late trade to end down 56 pfennigs at 70.59 marks after Moody's said it was cutting its long term deposit rating to AA1 from AAA.
The futures market was somewhat more active, with the March DTB DAX future up 11.5 points at 2,864.5. The December contract expired last week.
The outlook for Friday's trade was for similarly thin volumes. The earliest chance of some real activity, one dealer said, was next Monday, the last trading day of 1996.
